title: Infrastructure Weekly Update - GPU Fleet & Capacity (2026-03-02)
body:
Purpose:
Weekly infrastructure update focused on GPU fleet health, regional capacity, and near-term capacity planning for Q2. Intended audience: infra team, serving-runtime, solutions engineering (capacity requests).

Summary (TL;DR):
- Total fleet utilization (7d average): 78% overall.
- Headroom shrinking in us-east (current utilization 91% at peak hours) due to two new enterprise trial customers and a large batch job pattern.
- Action: Provision +40 H100-equivalent instances in us-east (spot + reserved mix) and enable aggressive prefix caching for identified workloads. PO draft ready, awaiting finance signoff.
- Planned maintenance: kernel + CUDA roll (3/07) for 4 racks in eu-west; will follow canary schedule.

Fleet snapshot (as of 2026-03-02):
- Global GPU pool (logical): 1,420 devices (H100-80GB equiv).
  - us-west: 480 devices (avg util 74%, 95p latency within SLO)
  - us-east: 380 devices (avg util 84%, peak 91% evenings UTC-5)
  - eu-west: 300 devices (avg util 69%)
  - ap-southeast: 160 devices (avg util 63%)
  - reserved-dedicated (customer-dedicated pools): 100 devices (util varies by customer; overall 55%)

Observations and recent incidents:
- 2026-02-28 22:10 UTC: short degradation in us-east batch scheduler causing ~12min queuing spike. Root cause: malformed slot accounting after recent scheduler change (PR #210). Rollback to stable scheduler resolved within 15m. Follow-up: add additional integration test for slot accounting (INF-4321).
- 2026-03-01: Increased pre-warming for canary LLMs triggered higher KV-cache pressure on some hosts. Observed transient OOMs on 6 hosts in us-west; kernel logs point to memory leak in pre-warm helper (assigned to Ethan).

Capacity planning (next 30 days):
- Q2 commitments: expected +140 H100-equivalent demand from two enterprise pilots (one long-tail chatbot, one embedding indexer).
- Proposal: immediate short-term purchase (cloud reserved instances + spot bursts) to add +40 H100-equivalent in us-east by 2026-03-10, and staged procurement of +100 H100-equivalent across us-west and eu-west by end of March.
- Rationale: mitigates current peak overloads and provides buffer for on-boarding. Detailed cost estimate attached in linked artifacts.

Meetings / decisions (capacity planning sync 2026-03-01):
- Attendees: Alicia Gomez (infra), Ethan Wu (platform-eng), Maya Chen (serving-runtime), Carlos Rivera (solutions-eng), Priya Shah (finance, joined for procurement).
- Key decisions:
  - Approve PO draft for short-term +40 H100-equivalent in us-east (Priya to get finance signoff by 2026-03-04).
  - Prioritize optimization work for the two pilot workloads: aggressive prefix caching and quantization suggestions from Optimize team (Maya to lead).
  - Schedule maintenance window 2026-03-07 for kernel/CUDA updates in eu-west; canary on 1 rack, then 3 racks.

Standup logs (high-level snippets, infra standups 2026-03-02):
- 09:15 UTC - Alicia: "PO draft done; waiting on Priya. Observability dashboards updated for us-east peaks. Need ops runbook reviewed before scaling."
- 09:17 UTC - Ethan: "Investigating pre-warm helper leak; reproduced locally. Hotfix candidate ready, will run canary on 3 hosts 12:00 UTC."
- 09:19 UTC - Maya: "Serving-runtime is ready to toggle aggressive KV-prefetch for pilot traffic; will coordinate with Ethan for hotfix window."
- 09:21 UTC - Carlos: "Solutions teams communicated expected onboarding timeline: staggered across 3 weeks, first payload arrives 3/12."

Action items (owner / due):
- Priya Shah (finance): finalize PO + approval for +40 H100 short-term capacity — due 2026-03-04.
- Ethan Wu (platform-eng): land hotfix for pre-warm helper memory leak; canary on 3 hosts 2026-03-02 12:00 UTC — due 2026-03-02 (in-progress).
- Maya Chen (serving-runtime): implement and validate aggressive KV-prefetch config for pilot workloads in staging — due 2026-03-05.
- Alicia Gomez (infra): update runbook for scale-up + failover steps and coordinate maintenance windows — due 2026-03-04.
- Carlos Rivera (solutions-eng): provide final onboarding ingestion profile from pilot customers (expected qps, batch sizes) — due 2026-03-06.

Risks / open questions:
- Procurement timeline: finance approval delay will push purchase into spot-only regime, raising cost and preemption risk. Mitigation: pre-authorize spot burst policy and reduce non-critical batch work.
- Cross-region routing: should we route excess us-east traffic to us-west vs. spinning up new reserved capacity? Tradeoffs: latency vs. cost. Need final policy from product/solutions. (Owner: Maya for proposal — due 2026-03-05).
- Long-tail model memory profile: early signs some models need >48GB GPU for stable KV-cache behavior. If confirmed, hardware mix adjustments required. (Experiment owner: Carlos).

Notes / links referenced:
- INF-4321: scheduler slot accounting test failure (linked)
- PR #210: scheduler change reverted after 2/28 incident (linked)
- Capacity cost estimate (confluence://capacity-planning/q2-2026)

Next steps / meeting cadence:
- Short daily standup for infra-platform working group (Mon-Fri 9:15 UTC) while pilots ramp.
- Capacity planning review 2026-03-04 to confirm finance outcome and procurement schedule.

Appendix: quick metric charts (text summary)
- 7d avg token throughput: 420M tokens/day (↑12% week-over-week).
- Median per-token CPU latency (routing layer): 18ms (SLO 25ms).
- 95p GPU queue time (us-east peak): 320ms (target <200ms) — primary painpoint.

If you want a shorter summary for execs, tell me and I'll extract a 1-paragraph blurb.

-- Alicia G.
